claim: Deep use of the envelope standard is visible in content-mode handling and in named extension attributes, not in copying the required attribute names.
query: CloudEvents binary vs structured content mode extension attributes tracing best practice
snippet: In binary content mode, the event data is placed into the HTTP request or response body as-is, with the datacontenttype attribute value declaring its media type in the HTTP Content-Type header; all other event attributes are mapped to HTTP headers. In structured content mode, event metadata attributes and event data are placed into the HTTP request or response body using an event format that supports structured-mode messages. Structured mode keeps event metadata and data together in the payload, allowing simple forwarding of the same event across multiple routing hops, and across multiple protocols. When including extension attributes when using binary content mode, make sure that their names consist of lower-case letters ('a' to 'z').

claim: Trace parentage does not survive asynchronous and cross-process agent hops on its own, which is why correlation has to ride on explicit attributes.
query: distributed tracing async agent workflows trace context propagation limits explicit correlation attributes long running 2026
snippet: When crossing async boundaries like threads or promises, trace context often doesn't automatically transfer because OpenTelemetry stores the current span in a context object tied to the current execution flow. When Agent A sends a message to Agent B, it must inject the current active context (trace ID) into the message headers or metadata, and Agent B must then extract this context and use it to start its own spans. If this isn't done, you will see two disconnected traces instead of one continuous workflow. To make traces queryable and actionable, you must enrich spans with semantic attributes.
title: Distributed tracing for agentic workflows with OpenTelemetry | Red Hat Developer

claim: The three named specifications compose as one layered format, current at a backward-compatible minor revision, and the verification procedure is part of the specification.
query: SLSA v1.1 in-toto attestation DSSE 2026 release status provenance specification
snippet: Version 1.1 is the current version. SLSA v1.1 is a minor release of SLSA where all changes are intended to be backwards compatible. Attestation format schema are clarified as informative and the specification texts (SLSA and in-toto attestation) are the canonical source of definitions. Additional updates include procedures for verifying VSAs and verifier metadata added to VSA format. In-toto attestations have two layers: the DSSE envelope and the statement, where DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope) is a lightweight container format for signed payloads. In-toto attestations are wrapped in DSSE for signing, which signs over the payload type and payload together using PAE (Pre-Authentication Encoding) to prevent confusion attacks.

claim: The standard is Standards Track, obsoletes its predecessor, and its extension members are the sanctioned way to carry what a caller must act on.
query: RFC 9457 problem details adoption 2026 API error standard type registry
snippet: RFC 9457 defines a "problem detail" to carry machine-readable details of errors in HTTP response content to avoid the need to define new error response formats for HTTP APIs. This document obsoletes RFC 7807. A problem type definition specifies additional members on the problem details object. For example, an extension might use typed links to another resource that machines can use to resolve the problem. Clients consuming problem details must ignore any such extensions that they don't recognize; this allows problem types to evolve and include additional information in the future. Problem type definitions specify the use of the Retry-After response header in appropriate circumstances.
title: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs Abstract

claim: The movement inside the window is registry-shaped: a closed set of type URIs, multiple problems in one response, and non-dereferenceable type URIs, not a change of format.
query: RFC 9457 problem details adoption 2026 API error standard type registry
snippet: It defines a single machine-readable error body, served as application/problem+json (or application/problem+xml), with five standard members: type, title, status, detail, and instance. Compared with 7807, Appendix D documents three additions: a registry for common problem-type URIs, clearer guidance on returning multiple problems in one response, and handling for non-dereferenceable type URIs. The formal registry hosted at IANA as well as the SmartBear Problems Registry act as valuable resources when determining what problem types are relevant for your APIs. As of 2026, this is the most widely adopted error format across major APIs including Stripe, GitHub, and Cloudflare.
title: Problem Details (RFC 9457): Doing API Errors Well

snippet: Returning a 503 Service Unavailable with a retryAfter extension member tells the client and infrastructure exactly how to handle the transient failure. By including retryAfter as an extension and ideally as a Retry-After HTTP header, you allow automated retry libraries to wait for the specified window. The type field is the resolved URI that clients use as the primary machine-readable identifier. The type field is a URI that uniquely identifies the error, enabling programmatic error handling.
